import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 236

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/236](https://www.erdosproblems.com/236)
-/

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace Erdos236

/--
$f(n)$ counts the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$.
-/
def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((List.range (Nat.log2 n + 1)).filter (fun k => Nat.Prime (n - 2^k))).length

/--
Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. Show that $f(n)=o(\log n)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_236: (fun n => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => Real.log (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos236

reformulations.difference: The source counts solution pairs (p,k), whereas Lean counts exponents in a finite list for which the natural-number remainder n − 2^k is prime.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every solution has p ≥ 2, hence 2^k < n and k ≤ Nat.log2 n, so the search includes every solution. Conversely, primality of n − 2^k forces 2^k < n, making natural subtraction exact and giving the solution p = n − 2^k. This prime is unique for each exponent, and the filtered range has no duplicates. At n = 0 both counts are zero. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved equality with the cardinality of {(p,k) | p.Prime ∧ n = p + 2^k}, proved that set finite, and proved the complete statement equivalent to the corresponding count/log(n) tending to zero.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k+p and some related problems, Summa Brasil. Math. 2 (1950), 113–123, especially pp. 113–115: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1950-07.pdf
review.notes: Both declarations are faithful. Erdős explicitly conjectures f(n) = o(log n) on p. 115 of the original paper, and the current problem page still records OPEN. Lean's atTop is on ℕ; log's values at 0 and 1 do not affect the asymptotic statement. Scratch checks compile without errors or warnings, and the equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Independent pair enumeration agrees with f for every 0 ≤ n ≤ 256, and all 105 published OEIS terms agree. The problem pages, OEIS entry, and original paper were read through the r.jina.ai text proxy. The reviewed file was not modified.
